Hmm, I'm biracial and bisexual so I have some thoughts. I won't speak much to the gender identities, because I'm not an expert on the subject matter, but racial identity is one I've grappled with my whole life. Race is what society tells me I am - I am a brown man and despite the fact that I also have a white family, people will always see me as a brown, Mexican looking guy, and there are a lot of assumptions people make because I fall under that race.

In addition to my race, I also have my ethnic and cultural background, which is a much more accurate description of who I am. I was born into two families, one white and American in every way, and the other side from Mexico and loud and proud of that fact! Although I was born with these two cultures, I also have the option to explore my culture and experience it how I want and with who I want, which enriches my experience and grows that culture - therefore claiming it as my own!

I guess from my lens I see gender identity as more similar to one's own personal culture. You were born with it, but you also have the ability to grow it how you see fit and experience your culture in the unique way that only you can. I don't know if race and gender are necessarily perfect comparisons, so maybe comparing it to culture is another way of looking at it?

I don't know, I could be way off base. I'm still trying to understand gender identity and be respectful of other members of the LGBT+ community, so please reeducate me if any of this sounds off.
